sections.title: What is LIC Jeevan Utsav Plan 771?

content.text: LIC Jeevan Utsav (Plan 771) is a non-linked, non-participating, individual, whole-life savings insurance plan launched by the Life Insurance Corporation of India. Unlike traditional endowment policies that mature at age 60 or 75, Jeevan Utsav provides lifelong financial protection and guaranteed annual income up to age 100.

sections.title: Key Features & Guaranteed Additions (₹40 per ₹1,000 BSA)

content.text: LIC Jeevan Utsav combines capital security with two powerful contractual guarantees:

items: Contractual Guaranteed Additions (GAs): For every year you pay premiums during your PPT, LIC adds ₹40 for every ₹1,000 of your Basic Sum Assured. For a ₹10 Lakh policy with a 12-year PPT, you earn a guaranteed ₹40,000/year, totaling ₹4,80,000 in bonus additions.

Guaranteed 10% Lifelong Payout: Starting 2 years after your premium payment term ends, LIC pays you an annual income equal to exactly 10% of your Basic Sum Assured for the rest of your life (up to age 100).

Choice of Income Options: You can choose Option 1 (Regular Income Payout) to receive 10% annually, or Option 2 (Flexi Income Option) to let your income accumulate with LIC at a guaranteed 5.5% compounding interest rate per annum.
Tax-Free Returns: Annual income payouts and nominee death benefits qualify for tax exemption under Section 10(10D) of the Income Tax Act.

sections.title: How LIC Jeevan Utsav Premiums & Income Are Calculated
sections.description: Understanding the exact mathematical formulas used by LIC underwriters:

content.text:
1. Base Premium & Modal Discounts

Base premiums are calculated per ₹1,000 of Basic Sum Assured based on entry age and PPT. High Sum Assured (HSA) rebates are deducted for policies of ₹10L and above. Modal loading rebates apply: 2% rebate for Yearly mode and 1% rebate for Half-Yearly mode.

2. Total Guaranteed Additions Formula

Total GAs = (Basic Sum Assured / 1000) × 40 × Premium Paying Term

3. Annual Survival Income Formula

Annual Income = 0.10 × Basic Sum Assured

4. Flexi Income Compounding Formula

If payouts are left with LIC under Option 2, the accumulated pool grows according to: Accumulated Pool = Annual Income × [((1.055)^N - 1) / 0.055] where N is the number of years deferred.

items.title: Example 1: Age 30, ₹10L Cover, 12-Year PPT (Regular Income)
items.body:
Investor Profile: Rahul, age 30, wants a guaranteed pension after age 44.

Investment: Chooses a 12-year PPT with ₹10,00,000 Basic Sum Assured. Yearly premium is ~₹85,500 + GST. Total outgo over 12 years: ~₹10.26 Lakh.

Benefits: Rahul earns ₹40,000 GA per year for 12 years = ₹4,80,000 Total GAs. From age 44 onwards (after 2-year deferment), Rahul receives ₹1,00,000 every single year for life. Upon his death at age 85, his nominee receives ₹10L BSA + ₹4.8L GAs = ₹14.80 Lakh lump sum.

items.title: Example 2: Age 40, ₹20L Cover, 10-Year PPT (Flexi Income Option)
items.body:
Investor Profile: Priya, age 40, wants to build a flexible retirement fund.

Investment: 10-year PPT for ₹20,00,000 cover. Yearly premium: ~₹2,10,000. Total GAs earned: ₹8,00,000.

The Flexi Payout: Her 10% income is ₹2,00,000/year. She chooses to leave it with LIC for 10 years. Compounding at 5.5% p.a., her income pot grows to ₹25.74 Lakh. She can withdraw up to 75% of this pool anytime or keep it growing.

sections.title: LIC Jeevan Utsav vs Jeevan Umang (Plan 945) vs Jeevan Labh
sections.description: Comparing Jeevan Utsav against popular LIC savings and pension policies:

sections.title: Eligibility Rules, Riders & Policy Loan Terms

items: Min/Max Entry Age: 90 days minimum; maximum 65 years (varies by PPT: max 65 for PPT 5, max 59 for PPT 10, max 50 for PPT 16).
Minimum Sum Assured: ₹5,00,000 (increases in multiples of ₹25,000). No maximum limit.
Deferment Period: 2 years after PPT ends for Plan 771; 1 to 10 years choice for Plan 883.
Loan Facility: Available after paying 1 full year of premiums for PPT 5-9, or 2 full years for PPT 10-16. Up to 75% of surrender value for active policies.
Surrender & Paid-Up: Policy acquires surrender value after 1 or 2 years. Making a policy 'Paid-Up' reduces Sum Assured proportionally while retaining accrued GAs.

sections.title: Tax Benefits Under Income Tax Act

items: Section 80C Deduction: Premiums paid towards Plan 771 or Plan 883 qualify for tax deduction up to ₹1.5 Lakh per financial year.
Section 10(10D) Exemption: Annual 10% survival income payouts and nominee death claim payouts are completely tax-exempt, provided aggregate annual premiums across life policies do not exceed ₹5 Lakh.
GST Applicability: Standard LIC GST applies (4.5% in 1st policy year, 2.25% in renewal years).

items.q: What is the difference between LIC Jeevan Utsav Plan 771 and Plan 871?
items.a: Plan 871 was the earlier plan table code. LIC updated and active tables are Plan 771 (Limited Premium Payment) and Plan 883 (Single Premium Payment).

items.q: How much annual income is guaranteed under Jeevan Utsav?
items.a: LIC guarantees an annual survival benefit of exactly 10% of the Basic Sum Assured every year starting 2 years after your Premium Paying Term (PPT) ends, payable for life up to age 100.

items.q: What are the Guaranteed Additions in Plan 771?
items.a: LIC adds a guaranteed bonus of ₹40 for every ₹1,000 of Basic Sum Assured for each year of your premium paying term. For a ₹10 Lakh cover over 10 years, total GAs equal ₹4,00,000.

items.q: What is the Flexi Income Option in Jeevan Utsav?
items.a: Under Option 2 (Flexi Income), instead of withdrawing your 10% annual payout, LIC retains it in an interest-bearing pool that compounds at a guaranteed rate of 5.5% p.a. You can withdraw up to 75% of this pool at any time.

items.q: What happens if the policyholder dies during the premium term?
items.a: If death occurs during the PPT, the nominee receives the Sum Assured on Death plus all accrued Guaranteed Additions. LIC guarantees the death benefit will be at least 105% of total premiums paid.

items.q: What happens if the policyholder dies after the pension starts?
items.a: If death occurs after the survival income starts, the nominee receives the Basic Sum Assured plus all accumulated Guaranteed Additions as a lump sum payout.

items.q: Can I take a loan against my Jeevan Utsav policy?
items.a: Yes. Policy loans are available after 1 to 2 years of premium payments (depending on PPT). You can borrow up to 75% of the surrender value for active policies.

sections.title: Conclusion: Is LIC Jeevan Utsav Right for You?

content.text: LIC Jeevan Utsav (Plan 771) is one of the most attractive guaranteed income products available in India. For risk-averse investors seeking guaranteed lifelong income unaffected by stock market fluctuations, locking in a 10% annual return backed by the Government of India provides unmatched peace of mind.
